kicker: Many paths lead into the mist — no one has reached the end.
summary: Ask “what is AGI” before “when will it come”; and in your own work, keep taste, checking and responsibility.

quiz.q: One person says “AGI arrives in 2027”, another says “it's still far off”. What should you ask first?
options: What does each mean by AGI?
Which company is in the lead now?
quiz.explain: Each side may use a different ruler: jobs, a ladder of levels, a test, or the signature of a panel. Same word AGI, different definitions.

defs.label: Everyone has a definition
defs.art: Four water vessels along the edge of a wooden veranda as the moon sets: a celadon tea bowl, a split-bamboo trough, a bronze basin and a stone tsukubai; each holds a round moon in its water, and before each lies a small stone carved with the name of who defines it. Touch a vessel and more water is poured in; the surface ripples, stills, and the moon in it takes the shape of that definition: a coin with a square hole, a ladder, a ten-spoke wheel, a council's seal. A paper strip hung below the vessel says who says what, and one veil of mist lifts from the garden. With all four, four threads of moonlight join the same moon to the four waters.
defs.legend: AGI: AI as broadly capable as a person. Four groups measure it with four different rulers.
defs.prompt: Touch each name stone to pour the water

view.text: AGI is a highly autonomous system that outperforms humans at most economically valuable work. The ruler: work.
There is no single finish line: rank AI on a ladder by both skill and breadth, from “emerging” to “superhuman”.
AGI is AI as versatile as a well-educated adult, scored on 10 areas such as reading and writing, maths and memory. On this scale GPT-4 scores 27%, GPT-5 57%.
When OpenAI declares AGI, an independent expert panel will verify it; many money terms between the two companies hinge on that day.

common.text: Four rulers: OpenAI measures by jobs, DeepMind by a ladder of levels, the Hendrycks group by a test, Microsoft–OpenAI by the signature of a panel.

insight.text: Arguing about “when AGI comes” is often arguing about “what AGI is”. Ask for the definition before you believe a date.

tide.label: The rope that measures work
tide.art: A long scroll of sand at moonset. Drag the moon along its arc from high in the sky down to the western horizon: the bamboo pole on the right throws a shadow that grows to the left along a measuring cord marked evenly in hours, from 1 hour at the pole's foot to 16 hours out in the mist. When the shadow reaches a notch, the notch shows its hours. The lower the moon, the faster the shadow leaps; by today it runs on into the dawn mist.
tide.prompt: Drag the moon down past each mark
tide.legend: The pole's shadow = how long a task AI can do on its own. Drag the moon down: time runs on to today.

fact.text: Claude 3.7 Sonnet: tasks about 1 hour long.
An agent using GPT-5: about 2 hours 17 minutes.

milestones.label: The ruler runs out: METR has no tasks long enough to measure

fact.text: An early Claude Mythos Preview: at least 16 hours (estimated 8.5 to 55 hours).

horizon.text: If the trend holds, METR projects AI could handle month-long projects on its own before 2030.

insight.text: In one year, the tasks AI can do on its own (succeeding half the time) grew from about 1 hour to at least 16 hours.

detail.text: METR is an independent research group that measures with real tasks: programming, machine learning, cybersecurity. Real-world work is far messier.
In the same period, AI also reached gold-medal level at the International Mathematical Olympiad (Jul 2025).

fork.label: Three paths into the mist
fork.art: A fork in the stone path at moonset; at its end a stone sand table on a pedestal holds a whole garden of hills, fields, woods and walls. Three bamboo well-sweeps stand at the three mouths: speed, sharing, control. Pull one and the garden in the tray reshapes at once: terraced paddies holding slivers of sky, a wild pine wood, a ring wall rising, a gate opening wide, forty lantern dots crowding inside the wall or spreading over the whole tray; leave all three midway and mist fills it. Three bands of mist lie across the branches; touch one and it parts on a slip of paper.
fork.prompt: Drag the buckets of the three bamboo well-sweeps up and down

note.text: This is a thinking tool built by AI Zen, not a forecast.

scenarios.name: Wilderness
scenarios.text: Fast progress, loose fences: many inventions, but accidents and misuse spread like weeds too.

scenarios.name: Common garden
scenarios.text: Fast, widely shared, well fenced: what many hope for, but it needs rare cooperation between countries and companies.

scenarios.name: Walled garden
scenarios.text: Tight control, but benefits pile up in a few places: safer, while the gap between rich and poor widens.

scenarios.name: Terraces
scenarios.text: Slow progress; society adapts step by step. Close to the “AI as normal technology” view.

scenarios.name: A path through the mist
scenarios.text: Everything halfway. Some benefit, some risk; the outcome depends on each year’s choices.

fork.mistsLabel: Three slips: what people are guessing
fork.mistPrompt: Touch the mist on the paths: what people are guessing

view.text: Scenario: AI speeds up AI research itself and by late 2027 beats experts at most tasks; it has two endings, “race” and “slowdown”.

mists.who: The AI 2027 team itself · note, Nov 2025

view.text: The authors say 2027 is only the “most likely single year”; their median forecasts are later, with one author at 2030.
AI will seep in over decades like earlier big technologies; people keep control if they build enough resilience.

insight.text: The future of AI does not just arrive: its speed, its rules and how its benefits are shared are all chosen by people.

detail.text: Governments set the rules, companies choose the speed, users choose what to use. This tray is a simulation AI Zen built for thinking, not a forecast.

trays.label: Three trays of work
trays.art: Low over a wooden veranda at moonset, boards running toward the garden. Bottom left, a rattan basket holds eight pebbles engraved with tasks. Three stone trays recede on a diagonal: dry gravel nearest, one half under water at the pond's edge, the farthest sunk in mist under the moon. Pick up a pebble and throw it into a tray. With all eight placed, pull the blind's cord: early sun spills across the trays, the hollows where AI Zen would lay each pebble appear, and stray pebbles roll along dotted paths to their places.
trays.prompt: Drag each pebble and throw it into the tray you think is right ({n}/{total})
trays.why: Touch a pebble that moved to see why
trays.keys: Pick a pebble, then press 1, 2 or 3 to place it in a tray
trays.compare: Pull the blind: compare with AI Zen’s sorting
trays.match: You and AI Zen sorted {n}/{total} pebbles the same way

trays.name: Needs a person to answer for it

tasks.label: Write 20 headline options
tasks.why: Drafting many options is quick for AI; you still do the choosing.

tasks.label: Summarise 200 customer comments
tasks.why: Reading a lot and grouping ideas is a strength; spot-check a few original quotes.

tasks.label: Draft-translate a post into English
tasks.why: Good drafts; brand voice and wordplay still need a human edit.

tasks.label: Moodboard and concept images
tasks.why: Drafts are fast and cheap; images for real use need rights checks and a close look at details.

tasks.label: A finished, on-brand video ad
tasks.why: Single shots look great; keeping characters, product and pacing consistent is still hard.

tasks.label: Run a multi-week campaign alone
tasks.why: Agents handle longer chains of work every year, but hard-to-undo steps still need human sign-off.

tasks.label: Choose ideas that fit the brand's taste
tasks.why: Taste is an accountable choice, rooted in knowing customers and culture.

tasks.label: Answering for mistakes, keeping relationships
tasks.why: Clients and partners need a person who stands behind the commitment.

expertNote.text: This is AI Zen’s own sorting as of Oct 2026, informed by METR and WEF; it may change month to month.

insight.text: Two things AI cannot take yet: choosing by taste, and answering for the result. Invest in those.

detail.text: Alongside them: writing a clear brief (the instructions for a job), checking results yourself, and combining several AI tools. WEF (Jan 2025) forecasts that nearly 40% of core skills will change by 2030.

jobs.text: The same survey expects by 2030: 170 million new jobs, 92 million lost, a net gain of 78 million.
